Subject: Corvane children’s ibuprofen recall: what parents need to know

We know many families are concerned about the recall involving children’s ibuprofen. Here is exactly what the recall covers and what to do if you have this product at home.

The product is Corvane Pediatric Ibuprofen Oral Suspension 100 mg/5 mL (berry flavour), 120 mL. Only lots CV6114A and CV6114B, with expiry 08/2027, are affected. Please check the lot number on the bottom of the box first. Other lots are not included.

The problem is the printing on the oral dosing syringe supplied in these boxes, not the medicine. The ibuprofen suspension meets its specifications and is not contaminated. On the affected syringes, every graduation is labelled at half its true volume: the mark labelled 2.5 mL actually measures 5 mL, and the mark labelled 5 mL actually measures 10 mL. A caregiver following those markings could therefore give approximately twice the intended dose.

If you have one of these lots:

- Stop using the supplied syringe and discard it so it cannot be used again. Do not try to calculate a correction or use it to measure another dose.
- You can obtain a correctly marked replacement oral syringe from us free of charge, with no receipt required. We expect replacements from Northshore today, Monday, November 9, before noon.
- You may instead return the affected product for a full refund under the manufacturer’s recall.
- We will also be open this Saturday, November 14, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. for replacement syringes, returns and exchanges.

If your child may have received too much, or you are uncertain how much was given, call your local poison centre now, even if your child seems well. Do not give another dose until the poison centre or a doctor tells you it is safe. The advice has to be specific to your child: their weight, the amount and number of doses, when they were given, and their health history, including kidney problems, can all matter. An individual child cannot be safely assessed through Facebook comments.

Call 911 or go to the nearest emergency department immediately if your child is very sleepy or difficult to wake, is vomiting blood, is not peeing, or has a seizure. Do not wait for a reply online.

We received the manufacturer’s recall notice on the evening of November 6. We removed the remaining affected stock and posted notices at the pharmacy on the morning of November 7. We understand that families are asking why they were not called. These bottles were sold over the counter, and most purchases did not create a patient profile or provide us with a phone number, so we do not have contact information for most purchasers.

We are sorry for the fear and confusion this has caused. Please share this information with anyone who may have purchased these lots, and contact your poison centre or doctor directly with any concern about a dose your child received.
---
